claims.text: Claude only ever auto-loads CLAUDE.md itself, not a memory folder (so facts must be pulled into a file CLAUDE.md points to)
RUNLOG CLAUDE.md went from six thousand tokens to under a thousand (6,080 to 912), eighty-five percent smaller
Same process on other channel (faceless-yt): seventy-five percent smaller (3,782 to 933)
AiLORA rebuild only twenty-two percent smaller (2,338 to 1,820) because most content genuinely belonged
Every locked fact, gotcha and constant was still present after rebuild across all three repos (grep-verified, [OK] on every line)
The CLAUDE.md is loaded into every single session regardless of what you're working on (six thousand tokens per session)
Brand colors, TTS voice and launch thresholds lived only in the narrative CLAUDE.md, and the separate memory files did not have them
Claude Code ships an official Anthropic plugin with two tools: one captures session learnings into CLAUDE.md, the other audits CLAUDE.md quality and proposes fixes
Both official tools only add to CLAUDE.md; neither asks whether content belongs there
Anthropic shipped /checkup, which dedupes CLAUDE.md against what's checked in, splits a bloated one into nested files, and cleans unused skills and MCPs
/checkup reorganizes but doesn't ask what belongs; not one official tool, including /checkup, does delete-and-rebuild
Claude Code's creator (Boris Cherny) said the actual fix is to delete your CLAUDE.md every few months and only add back what the model struggles without
Deleting CLAUDE.md in a git repo is safe because the old version is one command away forever
AiLORA's CLAUDE.md described three files (status, decisions, dead ends) but only one (BELIEFS.md) existed, so content defaulted back into CLAUDE.md
Having memory files doesn't mean you can safely delete CLAUDE.md; only works if they hold facts, not history
Audit scan run against AiLORA's original CLAUDE.md returned zero hits despite real narrative being present (keyword list tuned to author's vocabulary)
/triage-memory classifies session learnings and routes them, and will not let you default to CLAUDE.md
/audit-claude-md scans for narrative creeping back in and confirms every file CLAUDE.md points to still exists
Author's global Claude Code memory system has a 'what not to save' list (don't save what git tracks or code shows) and a single MEMORY.md index loaded each session that points to other files
A CLAUDE.md that has grown for months reads like a changelog with dates and 'fixed a bug where' entries; commit history already covers changelog entries
Final render duration 7:46.5 (466.5s) and word count 1,277 verified; hook claims ~117 words
Hook: same result on two more repos, with two commands built and smoke-tested across all three repos
ffmpeg -shortest with overlay filter silently truncated the video track by several seconds in render_captions/render_mascot

result.evidence: The docs say: "Claude Code has two complementary memory systems. Both are loaded at the start of every conversation." The table shows CLAUDE.md files are "Loaded into: Every session", and auto memory is also "Every session (first 200 lines or 25KB)". The same page also covers AGENTS.md, .claude/rules/ and @imports. So "only ever auto-loads CLAUDE.md" is overstated. Claude also auto-loads its own auto-memory MEMORY.md, which lives in a memory folder under ~/.claude/projects/. The narrower point holds: a repo-level memory/*.md folder like this project's is not auto-loaded, and its facts must be reachable from CLAUDE.md. Suggested rewording: "Claude auto-loads CLAUDE.md, not your repo's memory/ folder."

memory/video_ideas.md:163 table: "CLAUDE.md (loaded every session) | 6,080 tokens (est.) | 912 tokens"; text says it "dropped 85%". CLAUDE.md:54 says "Last rebuilt 2026-08-20: 6,080 → 912 tokens." Arithmetic: 1-912/6080 = 85.0%. Independent check from git: the pre-rebuild CLAUDE.md (commit 5446865^) is 24,508 bytes, about 6,127 tokens at 4 chars/token. The rebuilt file (5446865) is 3,686 bytes, about 921 tokens. Both are consistent with the claim. The figures are estimates, not exact tokenizer counts, and the source labels them "(est.)".

The official memory docs say: "Both are loaded at the start of every conversation," and the comparison table lists CLAUDE.md files as "Loaded into: Every session". The loading is not conditional on the task. The 6,000-token figure is the channel's own measurement. /home/invii/faceless-yt-transformation/CLAUDE.md:54 records "Last rebuilt 2026-08-20: 6,080 → 912 tokens." That is a self-reported figure with no raw receipt, and "six thousand" is a fair rounding of it. Caveat: this applies to the project-root and user-level CLAUDE.md. Subdirectory CLAUDE.md files and .claude/rules path-scoped rules can load lazily, but that does not affect the claim for a root file.

The plugin claude-md-management v1.0.0 has author "Anthropic" in plugin.json and sits in the claude-plugins-official marketplace cache. Its description reads "Tools to maintain and improve CLAUDE.md files - audit quality, capture session learnings, and keep project memory current." The README lists two tools. The skill claude-md-improver has the purpose "Keep CLAUDE.md aligned with codebase" and the prompt "audit my CLAUDE.md files". The command /revise-claude-md has the purpose "Capture session learnings". I did not read the skill's SKILL.md body, so "proposes fixes" rests on the README and plugin description. Caveat on wording: "ships with Claude Code" is loose. The plugin is distributed through the official Anthropic marketplace and installed separately. The local cache shows it installed, not bundled in the binary. I did not check the docs for whether the marketplace is auto-added.

The faceless-yt commit e0efd90 message says: "CLAUDE.md rebuilt from scratch as an index + pipeline command reference + non-negotiable rules only: 3,782 -> 933 tokens (75% reduction)." I checked the file sizes in git. CLAUDE.md before the commit was 15,220 bytes, about 3,805 tokens at 4 bytes per token. After the commit it was 3,777 bytes, about 944 tokens. The 3,782 and 933 figures were presumably computed by the author's own tokenizer, not by me, but they are consistent with these sizes. 933 / 3,782 = 24.7%, a 75.3% reduction, so "seventy-five percent smaller" holds.

result.evidence: The claim is overstated. The tools mostly add, but both apply a belongs-here filter, and the improver flags stale or generic content already in the file. (1) claude-md-improver SKILL.md:98-112 says "Propose targeted additions only", but also "Keep it minimal - Avoid: Restating what's obvious from the code; Generic best practices already covered; One-off fixes unlikely to recur; Verbose explanations". (2) The improver's references/quality-criteria.md:95-110 lists "Red Flags" to find in an existing CLAUDE.md: "References to deleted files/folders", "Outdated tech versions", "Generic advice not specific to the project", "Duplicate info across multiple CLAUDE.md files". It also scores Conciseness and Currency, and it ends with "Propose concrete improvements". (3) revise-claude-md.md:34-35 tells the model not to add "Verbose explanations" or "Obvious information". The nearest true version is that neither tool prunes or deletes existing content, or asks whether the file should exist at all. Both are additive by design, and the improver only flags problems and proposes fixes after the user approves.

Repo sources agree on the figures. memory/video_ideas.md:163 gives 6,080 (est.) to 912 tokens and says "dropped 85%". CLAUDE.md:54 says the same. scripts/rebuild-your-claude-md/script.md:104 says 85%. The arithmetic gives 85.0%. The checker's byte-count check from git also fits. I found nothing in the repo that contradicts the claim. The only weakness is that the figures are estimates, not exact tokenizer counts, and the claim as worded does not say so. That does not contradict it.

The repo's own records show a spot-check, not an exhaustive grep of every fact. video_ideas.md:178 says faceless-yt's "Correctness check (9 facts spot-checked) and narrative-smell scan both came back clean". The RUNLOG check shown on screen (build_video.py:306-308) is three hand-picked [OK] lines: palette hex #0D0E12, TTS voice am_michael, CTR >=4%. The script itself calls it "a short list of real values". I found no receipt, such as a log or output file, of a full grep over every locked fact, gotcha and constant. I found no recorded check for AiLORA at all, and the note on the RUNLOG rebuild only says the spot-check came back clean. A sampled check of a few values per repo does not support "every locked fact, gotcha and constant" or "[OK] on every line" across all three repos.

I found no source text that contradicts the claim. The repo shows the 6,080 figure is a pre-rebuild estimate. The "every session" part matches the official docs wording the checker already cited. Searching the repo turned up two things.

- /home/invii/faceless-yt-transformation/memory/video_ideas.md:163 lists "`CLAUDE.md` (loaded every session) | 6,080 tokens (est.) | **912 tokens**". The figure is explicitly marked as an estimate, so "six thousand" is consistent with it. Narration should avoid presenting it as a precisely measured count.
- The 6,080 figure describes the old, pre-rebuild file (CLAUDE.md:54, "Last rebuilt 2026-08-20: 6,080 → 912 tokens"). The current file is about 912 tokens. This is only a problem if the script uses the present tense for the current file. In past tense ("was six thousand tokens") the claim holds.

I did not fetch the official docs in this pass. Per the checker's quote, root and user-level CLAUDE.md load every session. The lazy-loading exceptions it noted (subdirectory files and path-scoped rules) do not apply to a root file.

The faceless-yt commit e0efd90 message says "3,782 -> 933 tokens (75% reduction)". I checked the file sizes with git: CLAUDE.md was 15,220 bytes before the commit and 3,777 bytes after. That is a 75.2% reduction in bytes, which matches the claim. The arithmetic also holds, since 933/3782 = 24.7%. The claim names faceless-yt, and the commit is in that repo. I found nothing that contradicts it.

result.evidence: I found nothing that contradicts the claim. The plugin's SKILL.md says the claude-md-improver skill outputs a quality report first, then "makes targeted updates" after user approval. That covers "audits quality and proposes fixes", which the checker had only inferred from the README. The /revise-claude-md command file says "Update CLAUDE.md with learnings from this session" and shows proposed changes before applying them, which covers "captures session learnings into CLAUDE.md". The README lists exactly two tools. The author is Anthropic (Isabella He, isabella@anthropic.com). known_marketplaces.json maps claude-plugins-official to the repo anthropics/claude-plugins-official. The only weak point is the word "ships". The plugin is distributed through Anthropic's official marketplace and installed separately, not bundled in the binary. I did not check whether that marketplace is auto-added, so I'd suggest softer script wording such as "Anthropic publishes an official plugin", but that does not make the claim false.

The claim is overstated. I checked the memory files in git just before current_state.md was built (commit 5bd9efb^, pre-rebuild, 2026-08-20). The launch thresholds were already in memory/experiments.md under "## Thresholds (from CLAUDE.md launch plan)". That section lists "CTR: ≥4% pass, ≥6% strong", "AVD: ≥40-50%", "Outlier: 3x+ channel median" and the kill rules. The TTS voice was already in memory/pending_decisions.md line 22: "Voice Reversed 2026-08-15: ... Kokoro TTS, local, `am_michael`". Brand color was only partly covered. pending_decisions.md line 24 mentions the ground color `#0D0E12`, but the full Signal palette hex set (`#3FC7D8`, `#E64D8A`, `#F4F6F8`) was only in CLAUDE.md. The script's source note, memory/video_ideas.md:139, says the palette, voice and mascot orange "exist only in CLAUDE.md prose". It then concedes "one incidental, non-indexed mention of the voice buried inside a pending_decisions.md narrative row". It does not mention the thresholds in experiments.md. The rebuilt current_state.md (5bd9efb, 08:24) did later hold all three facts at lines 33, 40 and 63.
